TotalHipArthroplasty.Challenges_Point1: Bone Deformities: Irregular femur and acetabulum shapes
TotalHipArthroplasty.Challenges_Point2: Younger Patients: Higher chances of revision surgery
TotalHipArthroplasty.Challenges_Point3: Soft Tissue Changes: Muscular imbalance and tightness
TotalHipArthroplasty.Challenges_Point4: Higher Risk of Complications: Dislocations, fractures, and leg length discrepancy
TotalHipArthroplasty.Customized_Para: We offer personalized 3D surgical planning using CT-based imaging in our well-equipped hospitals to identify:

TotalHipArthroplasty.Approaches_Point2: Severe Dysplasia: Posterior approach for better visibility
TotalHipArthroplasty.Approaches_Point3: True Acetabulum Identification: Using key anatomical landmarks
TotalHipArthroplasty.Techniques_Point1: Medialization & Cotyloplasty: To position cup anatomically
TotalHipArthroplasty.Techniques_Point2: Subtrochanteric Osteotomy: Used in Crowe IV hips to correct length and rotation
TotalHipArthroplasty.Techniques_Point3: Soft Tissue Release: Improves mobility and reduces pain
TotalHipArthroplasty.Femoral_Point1: Modular implants like S-ROM and Metha short stem
TotalHipArthroplasty.Femoral_Point2: Options for customized prostheses in severe deformities

TotalHipArthroplasty.Complications_Point1: Sciatic Nerve Protection: Controlled leg lengthening and intra-op nerve monitoring
TotalHipArthroplasty.Complications_Point2: Avoiding Loosening: Use of uncemented components with bone grafting
TotalHipArthroplasty.Complications_Point3: Limb Length Correction: Subtrochanteric osteotomies or staged THA

LegLengtheningSurgery.WhatIs_Para: Limb Length Discrepancy (LLD) refers to a condition in which one leg is shorter or longer than the other, often caused by uneven bone growth. LLD may result in posture imbalance, joint pain, and walking difficulties. Surgical treatment is usually recommended when the discrepancy exceeds 1 inch (2.5 cm). Better to share medical reports with us for doctor’s opinion, and expected success rate of procedure before surgery…

LegLengtheningSurgery.Types_Shortening_Para: A section of the longer bone is removed, and the ends are joined to achieve a balanced length.
LegLengtheningSurgery.Types_Epiphysiodesis_Para: Used during childhood or adolescence, this technique limits growth in the longer leg by modifying the growth plate, allowing the shorter leg to catch up.

KnockKneesSurgery.PageSubtitle: Restore Alignment, Relieve Pain, Walk Freely Again
KnockKneesSurgery.Intro: Discover expert knock knees correction through advanced osteotomy surgery in India. Learn the benefits, procedure, recovery process, and how InDocsCare Medical Services can help restore your mobility and confidence.
KnockKneesSurgery.WhatIs_Para: Knock knees, or Osteotomy Surgery, is a condition where the knees angle inward and touch while the ankles remain apart. This results in the legs forming an outward curve (Figure 1). While mild cases may go unnoticed, more severe deformities can lead to:
KnockKneesSurgery.SurgeryNeed_Title: Is Surgery Necessary for Knock Knees?
KnockKneesSurgery.SurgeryNeed_Para: In growing children, guided growth surgery may correct the issue early. However, osteotomy surgery is the preferred solution for teenagers, pediatrics and adults who have completed bone growth and are experiencing discomfort or impaired function.
KnockKneesSurgery.Osteotomy_Title: 🛠️ What Is Osteotomy Surgery for Knock Knees?
KnockKneesSurgery.Osteotomy_Para: Osteotomy is a specialized orthopedic surgery where the leg bones are precisely cut and realigned to correct deformities. In the case of knock knees:
KnockKneesSurgery.Osteotomy_Point1: The surgeon repositions the bones of the knee (usually the femur or tibia).
KnockKneesSurgery.Osteotomy_Point2: The goal is to realign the lower limb, reduce knee joint pressure, and restore proper weight distribution.
KnockKneesSurgery.Benefits_Title: 🌟 Benefits of Osteotomy for Knock Knees
KnockKneesSurgery.Benefits_Point1_para: The legs become straighter, improving both appearance and mechanical function.
KnockKneesSurgery.Benefits_Point2_para: By redistributing the load on the knee joint, patients experience significant reduction in chronic pain.
KnockKneesSurgery.Benefits_Point3_para: Unlike total knee replacement, osteotomy preserves your natural joint, ideal for young and active individuals.
KnockKneesSurgery.Benefits_Point4_para: Patients often return to normal activities, sports, and exercise with greater ease and stability.
KnockKneesSurgery.Steps_Title: 🧬 How Is the Osteotomy Procedure Performed?
KnockKneesSurgery.Steps_Point1_intro: Take X-rays or CT scans, and plan the exact angles for bone correction.
KnockKneesSurgery.Steps_Point2_intro: The procedure is done under general anesthesia, ensuring you feel no pain.
KnockKneesSurgery.Steps_Point3_intro: The surgeon cuts the affected bone, repositions it, and realigns your leg.
KnockKneesSurgery.Steps_Point4_intro: Metal plates, screws, or external devices hold bones in the new position until healed (Figure 2).
KnockKneesSurgery.Recovery_Hospital: Most patients stay 2–4 days post-surgery for pain management and monitoring.
KnockKneesSurgery.Recovery_PT: Rehabilitation begins shortly after surgery and is vital to restore strength, flexibility, and balance.
KnockKneesSurgery.Recovery_Activities2: Most patients return to full activity within 3–6 months, depending on age and healing speed.
KnockKneesSurgery.Contact_Point1: Top orthopedic surgeons in India with extensive experience
KnockKneesSurgery.Contact_Point4: Complete care — from consultation to rehabilitation

InternalFixation.MainTitle: Internal Fixation for Fractures: A Modern Solution for Bone Healing
InternalFixation.PageSubtitle: Explore how internal fixation helps heal broken bones using advanced surgical techniques and implants like plates, screws, and rods. Learn about the benefits, types, and recovery process from InDocsCare Medical Services.
InternalFixation.WhatIs_Title: What Is Internal Fixation in Fracture Treatment?
InternalFixation.WhatIs_Para:
Internal fixation is a surgical method to stabilize broken bones from inside the body using medical-grade implants. Unlike traditional external casts and splints, internal fixation uses plates, screws, rods, or wires to keep the fractured bones properly aligned until they heal completely.
This advanced orthopedic technique promotes quicker recovery, reduces complications, and improves long-term outcomes for patients with moderate to severe fractures.
InternalFixation.Benefits_Title: Benefits of Internal Fixation for Bone Fractures
InternalFixation.Benefits_Point2: <bold>Early return to mobility and normal function</bold>
InternalFixation.Benefits_Point3: <bold>Reduced risk of improper healing (malunion or nonunion)</bold>
InternalFixation.Types_Title: Common Types of Internal Fixation Devices
InternalFixation.Plates_Para: <bold>Plates</bold> act like internal splints that hold fractured bones together. They are attached to the outer surface of the bone using<bold> surgical screws.</bold>
InternalFixation.Plates_Point1: Plates and screws may remain permanently or be removed later.
InternalFixation.Plates_Point2: Used in <bold>forearm, ankle,</bold> and other long bone fractures.
InternalFixation.Plates_Example: <bold>Example:</bold> X-ray shows a forearm fracture treated with plates and screws.
InternalFixation.Screws_Para: <bold>Screws</bold> are the most commonly used internal fixation device due to their versatility.
InternalFixation.Screws_Point1: Available in different sizes and designs
InternalFixation.Screws_Point2: Can be used alone or with rods and plates
InternalFixation.Screws_Point3: Sometimes removed post-recovery, depending on the case
InternalFixation.Screws_Example: </bold>Example: </bold>X-ray shows an ankle fracture stabilized using screws and plates.
InternalFixation.Rods_Para: <bold>For long bone fractures</bold> (like the femur or tibia), <bold>rods or nails</bold> are inserted into the bone marrow canal.
InternalFixation.Rods_Point1: Screws at both ends lock the rod and prevent rotation or shortening
InternalFixation.Rods_Point2: Typically used for<bold> thighbone (femur) and shinbone (tibia) </bold>fractures
InternalFixation.Rods_Example: <bold>Example: </bold>Healed shinbone fracture treated with an intramedullary nail (X-ray).
InternalFixation.Pins_Para: <bold>Pins or wires </bold>are ideal for small bone fractures or pediatric cases.
InternalFixation.Pins_Point1: Used when screws or plates are too large
InternalFixation.Pins_Point2: Can be combined with other fixation methods
InternalFixation.Pins_Point3: Often <bold>removed after healing</bold>, though in some cases left in permanently
InternalFixation.Pins_Example: <bold>Example:</bold> Child’s elbow fracture held in place with two surgical pins.
InternalFixation.Risks_Intro: While internal fixation surgery is generally safe, it does carry certain risks:
InternalFixation.Risks_Point3: Hardware failure or deformation over time
InternalFixation.Risks_Factor1: The<bold> location and severity</bold> of the fracture
InternalFixation.Risks_Factor3: <bold>Post-surgical care</bold> and adherence to recovery instructions
InternalFixation.Conclusion_Title: Conclusion: A Reliable Method for Fracture Management
InternalFixation.Conclusion_Para:
Internal fixation is a proven and effective solution for treating bone fractures that require surgical stabilization. At InDocsCare Medical Services, our orthopedic surgeons use advanced techniques and personalized care to ensure optimal healing and quicker recovery for our patients.

If you or a loved one has suffered a serious fracture, book a consultation with our orthopedic team to explore internal fixation and other modern treatment options.

In many cases, early diagnosis and treatment can help improve hand function and quality of life.

CongenitalHandDeformities.Types_Point4_para: Unusually short fingers due to abnormal bone growth.
CongenitalHandDeformities.Types_Point5_para: Missing central fingers, creating a claw-like hand appearance.

CongenitalFootDeformities.MainTitle: Congenital Foot Deformities in Children: Types, Causes & Treatment Options
CongenitalFootDeformities.PageSubtitle: Explore the causes, types, and treatment options for congenital foot deformities in children. Learn about clubfoot, webbed toes, cleft foot, and more. Expert care from InDocsCare Medical Services.
CongenitalFootDeformities.WhatIs_Para:
Congenital foot deformities are structural abnormalities in the feet present at birth. These conditions can affect one or both feet and may impact the bones, muscles, tendons, or skin. They range from mild to severe and may affect your child’s ability to walk, run, or perform daily activities.
At InDocsCare Medical Services, our pediatric orthopedic specialists are experienced in diagnosing and treating a wide range of congenital foot deformities through personalized care plans that include both non-surgical and surgical treatments.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type1_Para: One of the most common foot deformities, <bold>clubfoot</bold> causes the baby’s foot to twist downward and inward. It may affect one or both feet and is usually visible at birth.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type1_Cause: <bold>Cause: </bold>Abnormal development of bones, tendons, and muscles during pregnancy
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type1_Treatment: <bold>Treatment:</bold>The<bold> Ponseti method</bold> (gentle stretching and casting) is effective in most cases. Severe deformities may require surgery.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type2_Para: In <bold>syndactyly,</bold> two or more toes are fused together by skin, tissue, or bone.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type2_Treatment: <bold>Treatment :</bold> Often cosmetic surgery is considered if mobility or shoe fit is affected
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type3_Para: A rare condition where the middle of the foot is split, giving it a “lobster claw” appearance. It may involve missing toes or a deep V-shaped cleft.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type3_Cause: <bold>Cause: </bold>Often genetic, and sometimes part of syndromes like<bold> EEC</bold>
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type3_Treatment: <bold>Treatment: </bold>Surgery may be performed to improve appearance and function; custom shoes may also help
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type4_Para: In this deformity, the toes curl abnormally — upward at the base and downward at the joints — creating a claw-like shape.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type4_Cause: <bold>Cause: </bold>Nerve damage, trauma, arthritis, or tight shoes
CongenitalFootDeformities.Type4_Treatment: <bold>Treatment: </bold>Stretching, orthotics, or surgery in severe cases
CongenitalFootDeformities.HowCommon_Title: How Common Are Congenital Foot Deformities?
CongenitalFootDeformities.HowCommon_Note: Severity can vary widely even among family members with similar genetic traits.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Causes_Point1: <bold>Genetic mutations </bold>(inherited conditions like clubfoot or syndactyly)
CongenitalFootDeformities.Causes_Point4: <bold>Environmental exposures</bold> such as smoking or pollution during pregnancy
CongenitalFootDeformities.Causes_Note: Early prenatal care and avoiding harmful substances during pregnancy may help reduce risk.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Diagnosis_Para: Diagnosis usually begins at<bold> birth</bold> or during a<bold> routine prenatal ultrasound</bold>. A thorough<bold> physical examination</bold> is conducted, followed by imaging tests if necessary:
CongenitalFootDeformities.Diagnosis_Note: These tests help assess the severity and guide treatment planning.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Treatment_Title: Treatment Options for Congenital Foot Deformities
CongenitalFootDeformities.Treatment_Para: Treatment depends on the type and severity of the condition. At<bold> InDocsCare</bold>, we provide both <bold>non-surgical</bold> and <bold>surgical </bold>interventions.
CongenitalFootDeformities.NonSurgical_Point3: <bold>Custom orthotic devices</bold> like braces or special footwear
CongenitalFootDeformities.NonSurgical_Note: These are often effective for mild to moderate deformities.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Surgical_Point1: Complex or severe deformities (e.g., cleft foot, rigid clubfoot)
CongenitalFootDeformities.Surgical_Note: Surgery aims to <bold>realign bones, adjust tendons,</bold> and improve both function and appearance.
CongenitalFootDeformities.Goals_Point3: Improve quality of life and self-confidence
CongenitalFootDeformities.Goals_Note: Our goal is to ensure your child can live an<bold> active, pain-free life,</bold> participating in school and play like any other child.

CongenitalFootDeformities.CTA_Para: If your child shows signs of a foot deformity, don’t wait. Early diagnosis and treatment can make a <bold>life-changing difference.</bold> Contact <bold>InDocsCare Medical Services </bold>today to schedule a personalized consultation with our specialists.
